alex.sre: Heads-up — planned weekend change to per-route concurrency caps + a small canary load test. Please read; we need oncall + infra eyes.

alex.sre: Window: Sat 2025-07-19 02:00-05:00 UTC. Intent: reduce p99 latency regressions seen on long-tail prefix traffic by lowering per-route concurrency for non-critical routes and exercising autoscaler behavior under lower concurrency.

alex.sre: What we'll do:
- Apply temporary per-route concurrency cap change for routes tagged `route.class=background` from 120 -> 60.
- Launch canary load test (traffic generator) against a small subset (10%) of background routes for 30m mid-window.
- Leave dedicated/reserved-customer routes untouched (routes with `customer.tier=dedicated`).

alex.sre: Config snippet we'll push (will be visible in infra-change job):
```yaml
- selector: route.class=background
  action: set_concurrency
  value: 60
  dry_run: false
```

alex.sre: Monitoring & rollback:
- Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/route-concurrency and https://dash.redwood.internal/d/autoscaler-health
- Alerts will be tightened for the window: p99 latency > 2s on any canary route OR error rate > 0.5% triggers immediate rollback.
- Rollback plan: ops-automation job will revert concurrency to 120, and the load generator will be shut down.

alex.sre: Who's needed: oncall (devon), infra (maria), anyone owning autoscaler (jamie). Please ack below.

maria-prodops: Ack. I'll update the runbook and stay on standby 01:30-05:30 UTC.

devon-oncall: Ack — I'll watch the p99 dashboard and ensure alerts route to #eng-oncall. I’ll prepare a quick runbook note for manual rollback in case automation fails.

jamie-eng: Quick Q: are any customer routes that are served from dedicated pools impacted? I want to ensure we don't touch SLA-backed tenants.

alex.sre: Good question — no. We filter by `customer.tier!=dedicated` so dedicated pools are excluded. Only public/hosted background routes.

ops-automation: Scheduled job created: `change-concurrency-1769999001` — will run 2025-07-19T02:05:00Z. Watch job logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/1769999001/logs

sre-bot: Reminder posted to #eng-oncall 30m before window.

maria-prodops: :thumbsup: also adding a short smoke test to verify KV cache warmup doesn't regress after change.

jamie-eng: If autoscaler spin-up looks slow, do we want to temporarily bump mitigate via burst-cap? Or do we want the canary to surface that?

alex.sre: For this test we want to observe autoscaler behavior under the lowered cap; we have a fallback burst-cap policy if error rate climbs. We will not pre-bump.

devon-oncall: Noted. I'll keep escalation path ready and will call paging policy if alerts exceed threshold.

alex.sre: Post-test: ops will publish a 1-paragraph summary in #eng-sre and a short incident-style note in the runbook if anything unexpected happens. Expected: no customer-visible impact.

maria-prodops: Thanks — I'll also capture metric diffs and token-cost delta for the change window.

jamie-eng: Ack.

devon-oncall: Ack.

alex.sre: Thanks everyone. If you spot anything odd before the window, ping me directly.

maria-prodops: Closing note — will also notify support to expect any escalations from hosted customers, though we do not anticipate any.
